Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 7H I -1973 




Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1 997 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
INSERTER, STAPLE, ORTHOPAEDIC 



1. Scope — Specifies dimensions and other requirements for staple inserter used for inserting the 
staples in the bone. 

2. Material — Stainless steel bars conforming to Designation 30CM3 or 20CM3 of IS : 6603-1972 
' Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 . 
r- 19 DIA r-19DIA 



r22 OIA 





All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 INSERTER, STAPLE, ORTHOPAEDIC 

4. Heat Treatment — The inserter shall be hardened and tempered to 400 to 450 HV. 

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 The inserter shall have the recess to hold the staple. 

5-2 It shall have a screw hole for flat head screw to keep the staple in position. A spare screw shall 
also be supplied. 

5.3 The inserter shall be free from pits, burrs, draw-marks, cracks and other surface contaminations. 

5.4 It shall be passivated and polished bright. 

5.5 The screw threads shall be neat and clean. 

6. Corrosion Resistance Test — Scrub the instrument with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water 
and then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the instrument, immerse in copper sulphate solution at 
room temperature for 6 minutes and wash with fresh water or wet cotton wool. 

The copper sulphate solution shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuS0 4 .5H 3 ) 4'0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H 2 S0 4 ) (sp gr 1-84) 10'0 g 

Distilled water [see IS : 1070-1960 'Specification for 90'0 ml 
water, distilled quality ( revised) ' ] 

There shall be no red stains or spots on the instrument, but dulling of the polished surface may 
be permitted. 



Adopted 20 December 1973

7. Marking — The inserter shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution, New 
Delhi 110001. 

8. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
